standard.title: Use visual conventions and materials to create artworks
standard.description: use visual conventions, visual arts processes and materials to create artworks
standard.prior_knowledge: Students can create artworks that communicate ideas using materials and play (AC9AVAFC01). They have begun making deliberate choices about what to include and why. They have not yet used visual conventions deliberately or selected processes to serve specific communicative intentions.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students use visual conventions, visual arts processes and materials to create artworks, making deliberate choices about how these elements work together.

nodes.label: What visual conventions are
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can identify and name basic visual conventions — line, shape, colour, texture — and recognise how they are used in artworks.
nodes.minimum_width: Name at least two visual conventions (e.g. line, colour, shape, texture) and identify them in an artwork or the environment.
nodes.typical_width: Identify and name a range of visual conventions (line, shape, colour, texture, pattern, space) in artworks, the environment and their own making; distinguish between open lines and closed shapes.
wider: Observe how visual conventions are used in artworks and designs by First Nations Australians — identify colours, symbols and patterns with guidance from culturally authoritative resources
Go on a 'line hunt' — photograph or sketch different types of lines in the school environment and categorise them
nodes.hinge_reason: Students who cannot name and recognise visual conventions cannot use them deliberately in making — the vocabulary enables the intentionality that all subsequent creating nodes require.

response_modes.reason: Visual convention vocabulary needs to accumulate across many encounters in making, looking and environment. Students who have seen conventions named in only one or two contexts develop fragile recognition.

success_criteria: Names at least two visual conventions correctly
Identifies those conventions in at least one artwork or environmental example

nodes.label: Experimenting with materials and processes
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can experiment with a range of materials and visual arts processes to discover what effects are possible.
nodes.minimum_width: Try at least two materials or processes; describe one effect discovered.
nodes.typical_width: Experiment with a range of materials and processes (mark-making, printing, layering, 3D construction, digital tools); explore accidental and intentional effects; reflect on what each material can do.
wider: Explore layering as a visual technique — build a surface using pastels, then watercolour, ink and wax; identify how each layer changes the work
Combine digital and analog tools in one experiment — use a drawing app alongside traditional media and compare what each can do

response_modes.reason: Students who experiment with only one or two materials develop limited material vocabulary. A wider range of processes (printing, layering, 3D, digital) reveals that different materials serve different communicative purposes.

nodes.width_opportunity_reason: Digital/analog combination and layering techniques are particularly rich — students who explore these discover how material choice shapes meaning, which feeds directly into intentional creating.
success_criteria: Experiments with at least two different materials or processes
Describes at least one effect discovered — what the material or process can do

nodes.label: Using conventions and materials to create
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can select and use visual conventions, processes and materials deliberately to create an artwork.
nodes.minimum_width: Create an artwork that uses at least one named visual convention and one chosen process or material deliberately.
nodes.typical_width: Create artworks using combinations of visual conventions, processes and materials; make and explain choices about how these elements serve the work's communicative intent; include both analog and digital options.
wider: Create an artwork that combines digital and analog art-making — respond with colour, line and shape to music to communicate how the music makes you feel
Use 3D construction methods to represent an idea from another learning area — select materials (modelling clay, found objects) based on what the work needs to communicate
Create a collagraph or relief print — select textures and materials deliberately to produce a specific visual effect

response_modes.reason: Students bring together their understanding of conventions and their material experimentation to create with deliberate intent. The coordinating move — choosing elements because they serve the work — is the integration point.

success_criteria: Creates an artwork using at least one named visual convention deliberately
Can explain why they chose a particular material, process or convention for this work
